html:
The guerrilla leader who led Zimbabwe from its independence in 1980 until he was forced out in 2017, first as prime minister and from 1987 as president.

A teacher by training, he was jailed for ten years by the white minority government of Rhodesia under Ian Smith. Freed in 1974, he led the ZANU movement's war from Mozambique in the Rhodesian Bush War. The Lancaster House Agreement of 1979 ended the war, and he won the 1980 election.

He began with talk of reconciliation and invested in schools and health. But in the Gukurahundi campaign of 1983 to 1987, his army's Fifth Brigade killed thousands of civilians in Matabeleland. From 2000 his fast-track land reform seized white-owned farms, often violently. Farm output fell, the economy collapsed, and hyperinflation wiped out savings. He held on through disputed and violent elections until the army removed him in November 2017. He died in 2019.
sum: The guerrilla leader who led Zimbabwe from its independence in 1980 until he was forced out in 2017, first as prime minister and from 1987 as president.
